lines.trans: First into the tin goes the COMPLETE berry almond cake recipe—both halves together!
Did you seal it in waterproof plastic AND write HONEY AND ORANGE ZEST in capitals?!
Future bakers thirty summers from tonight deserve zero ink smudges and zero soup ladles!
Next, here is a clean signed copy of our Courtyard Waltz and four-hand duet.
And from Rami and me: birch clothespin number nine, signed on the back by everyone!
Oh, look what our Room Eight mapmaker just sent in with Suad to add on top!
While we played piano, he sketched all twenty-eight of us under the rooftop lanterns!
Look at Tariq standing by the doorway pretending not to smile in charcoal!
Tuck a small packet of dried courtyard mint leaves in the corner for a sweet smell.
Thirty summers from now, someone will lift this lid and smell warm summer tea.
Lid pressed down snug, white cloth tape around the rim—ready for the waxed linen!
Let us carry it out under the lanterns while the third stone is still waiting!

Let us carry it out under the lanterns while the third stone is still waiting!
Goodbye!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Form IV hollow verb (بضيف / ضفت). Used for adding an item to a box, list, or recipe.

examples.text: كل واحد بيضيف تذكار صغير للعلبة.
examples.trans: Everyone adds one small keepsake to the tin.
We added a little honey and orange zest.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian Form X verb (بيستاهل / بتستاهل) meaning 'to deserve, be worth it'.

examples.trans: The ovens deserve a break after baking!

examples.text: انتي بتستاهلي كل خير يا سلمى.
examples.trans: You deserve every good thing, Salma.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: برتقالات.

examples.trans: The fresh orange juice is cold.
We bought oranges and apples from the market.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of برش ('to grate'). Used in baking for citrus zest (برش البرتقال 'orange zest', برش الليمون 'lemon zest').

examples.text: برش البرتقال بيعطي الكيكة ريحة حلوة.
examples.trans: Orange zest gives the cake a lovely aroma.
We added one teaspoon of lemon zest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببعت, بيبعت).

examples.trans: Last week I sent him a postcard.
She sent a kind thank-you note.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine loanword for plastic wrap, sleeves, or containers.

examples.text: غلّفت الوصفة ببلاستيك عشان ما تتبلل.
examples.trans: She sealed the recipe in plastic so it would not get wet.

examples.text: ما بنحب نحط الشاي بكاسات بلاستيك.
examples.trans: We do not like serving tea in plastic cups.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Used to contrast two different situations or actions happening at the same time.

examples.text: بنرتب القاعة بينما بتبرد الكيكة بالظل.
examples.trans: We tidy the hall while the cake cools in the shade.

examples.text: طلعنا الساحة بينما الحجرة التالتة بتستنى.
examples.trans: We carried it out while the third stone is waiting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تالتة, plural: تالتين).

examples.trans: The attic room is on the third floor.
He used to sit on the third step.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian all-purpose word for 'all set, fine, spot-on!'.

examples.trans: Everything has to be spot-on!
Alright, I can remember the sentences.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the rim of a tin or the edge of a paving stone (الحافة الشمالية 'the north edge'). Plural: حواف.

examples.trans: We wrapped white tape around the rim of the tin.
Lower the north edge first gently.

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: Standard Arabic and colloquial term for ink used in pens.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبازين.

examples.trans: The baker opens the oven at five in the morning.
The bakers' market is near the overpass.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Temporal preposition meaning 'during' (خلال عزفنا 'during our playing') or 'within' (خلال ساعة 'within an hour').

examples.trans: During our piano playing, he sketched all of us!

examples.text: بنخلص ترتيب الساحة خلال عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: We will finish tidying the courtyard within ten minutes.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Geminate Form I verb (بدس / دسّيت). Used for tucking a small packet or note neatly into a corner.

examples.trans: Tuck a small packet of dried mint in the corner.
I slipped the letter under the room door.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Intensive occupation noun from رسم ('draw/paint'). رسام خرايط means 'mapmaker/cartographer'.

examples.text: رسام الخرايط قعد على طاولة واحد.
examples.trans: The mapmaker sat down at table one.

examples.text: هاد الرسام عمل لوحة رائعة للشارع.
examples.trans: This artist made a wonderful painting of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: A noun referring to a single drawing, illustration, or painting.

examples.text: في رسمة مفتاح دهبي فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a drawing of a golden key above the door.
His pencil sketches are very detailed.

meanings.note: Standard verb for lifting something up or raising.

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: روايح.

examples.trans: The aroma of coffee in the morning is wonderful!
The scent of cinnamon reaches the second floor.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطوح.

examples.trans: We heard the sound of rain on the roof.
From the rooftop we see the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'together'.

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
We drank morning coffee together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشم, بيشم).

examples.trans: Smell that wonderful aroma in the kitchen!
We smelled the cinnamon from the stairs.

meanings.note: Collective noun for wax or candles.

examples.text: لفينا العلبة بقماش شمع العسل الأصفر.
examples.trans: We wrapped the tin in yellow beeswax cloth.
We put small candles beside the lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شوربات.

examples.trans: Here is a cup of hot vegetable soup.
Hot soup is wonderful on a rainy day.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Preposition meaning 'against' or 'resistant to / -proof' (ضد المي 'waterproof', ضد الهوا 'windproof').

examples.trans: We sealed the recipe in waterproof plastic.

examples.text: مشابك الغسيل الخشب ضد الهوا القوي.
examples.trans: The wooden clothespins are proof against strong wind.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عريضة, plural: عراض).

examples.trans: The wide desk under the window is comfortable.
There are wide wooden beams in the ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Piano playing calms the nerves.
Whenever she finishes playing, she smiles.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Can refer to a cardboard box, a tin can, or a small container.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
I saved this old wooden box.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The clean sheets are in the linen closet.
We hung the laundry in the morning sun.

meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cover, or sometimes a blanket.

examples.trans: Put the lid on the pot.
In winter I sleep under a heavy blanket.

meanings.en: to wrap; to cover; to seal in a cover
meanings.note: Form II verb from root غ-ل-ف (same root as غلاف 'cover/envelope').

examples.trans: We wrapped it in wax paper.
We need to wrap the gift before the party.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for charcoal (for grilling or sketching); a single piece is فحمة.

examples.trans: A quick charcoal sketch will do.
We lit the charcoal for grilling in the garden.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كياس.

examples.trans: Give me a cloth bag for the shop.
I carried the bag of apples and bread.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word (lazzaaq) for sticky tape or electrical tape (لزاق كهربا).

examples.text: لف طارق السلك الجديد بلزاق كهربا أسود.
examples.trans: Tariq wrapped the new wire with black electrical tape.

examples.text: عندك لفة لزاق بالمكتب يا نور؟
examples.trans: Do you have a roll of tape at the desk, Nour?

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Active participle of ابتسم ('to smile').

examples.text: أبو طارق وقف بنص الساحة مبتسم ومبسوط.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq stood in the middle of the courtyard smiling happily.

examples.text: نور بتستقبل الضيوف الصبح بوجه بشوش ومبتسم.
examples.trans: Nour greets guests in the morning with a warm, smiling face.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from root ج-ف-ف ('dry'), used for dried flowers, herbs, and leaves.

examples.trans: There are dried olive leaves in them too.
We drink dried sage in the winter.

meanings.note: Form X passive participle of استقبل ('to face what comes ahead'); used as a masculine noun meaning 'the future'.

examples.trans: This letter is for future Rami.

examples.text: ما حدا بعرف شو مخبّي المستقبل.
examples.trans: Nobody knows what the future holds.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Instrumental noun from شبك ('fasten/clip'): names a shutter catch/hook or paper clip.

examples.text: ثبتنا الشيش عالحيط بمشبك حديد أسود ماكن.
examples.trans: We secured the shutter against the wall with a sturdy black iron catch.

examples.text: تأكد إن المشبك مسكر منيح قبل ما تهب الريح.
examples.trans: Make sure the catch is latched tightly before the wind blows.

meanings.note: Passive participle of ضغط ('to press/squeeze'), used for tight-fitting covers or packed schedules.

examples.trans: The box lid is pressed snug and tight.
My schedule is very packed this week.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Noun of instrument (مَفْعَلة) from غرف ('to scoop/ladle out'); pl. مغارف.

examples.trans: Bring me the big ladle.
He ladled the soup with a wooden ladle.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of وقّع ('to sign a document, check, or letter'), root و-ق-ع.

examples.trans: The little notebook is signed by Suad.
The paper is signed and stamped, ready.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from نسخ ('to copy'); used for photocopies, spare keys, or book editions. Plural: نسخ.

examples.trans: There's a second copy inside the house.
Make me a copy of the key.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for clean or tidy.

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the room is ready.

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water onto your clean floor.

meanings.note: A very common herb used in Levantine tea and cuisine.

examples.trans: Tea with fresh mint warms the heart.
We planted mint in the courtyard beside the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Used for both a doctor's prescription and a cooking recipe.

examples.text: بدّي أسجّل كل وصفة في الدفتر.
examples.trans: I want to write down every recipe in the notebook.
This is my grandmother's recipe for maqluba.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!
